summary: AdMob web-safety regression PASSED. Backend: 26/26 pytest tests pass (unchanged suite in /app/backend/tests/test_meets.py). react_native_issues.issue: Pre-existing (non-blocking) deprecation warning. Reference: /app/frontend/app/live.tsx:7 and /app/frontend/app/control.tsx:7. Recommend migrating to react-native-safe-area-context.

critical_code_review_comments: AdMobBanner.web.tsx correctly returns null so Metro's web bundle never touches react-native-google-mobile-ads — verified: no bundle error, admob-banner testID absent on web.
live.tsx imports AdMobBanner via '@/src/components/AdMobBanner' and renders <AdMobBanner /> after </ScrollView>; on web the .web.tsx stub resolves and renders null — verified.
control.tsx does NOT import AdMobBanner (grep confirmed) — matches spec that banner shows only on parent live board.
server.py public_meet() correctly strips passcode from GET /api/meets/{code} and GET /api/meets/id/{id}/read (26/26 backend tests confirm).
AdMobBanner.tsx uses Constants.executionEnvironment === ExecutionEnvironment.StoreClient to guard against Expo Go — sound approach; native prod build path will still initialize mobileAds().

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested web flows (live board loads, admob absent on web, advance/previous, live-viewers, copy link, announcements + dismiss, favorite toggle)

rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. The previously-reported Metro bundle crash caused by importing react-native-google-mobile-ads on web is resolved by /app/frontend/src/components/AdMobBanner.web.tsx returning null; Metro's platform-specific resolver picks the .web.tsx variant for web builds so the native module is never referenced.
